title: CAN WE TRUST AI BENCHMARKS? AN INTERDISCIPLINARY REVIEW OF CURRENT ISSUES IN AI EVALUATION

bias_targets.methodology: Meta-review of existing AI evaluation literature, highlighting how current safety benchmarks and capability tests disproportionately focus on English content while lacking multilingual evaluation.
Literature review examining how benchmark datasets are often abstracted from their social contexts, perpetuating Anglo-centric perspectives and under-representing minority views.

Critiquing the construct validity of existing gender fairness benchmarks (e.g., WinoGender, WinoBias) and analyzing the historical use of problematic datasets (e.g., the sexualized Lena test image) in computer vision.

Analyzing the epistemological claims of standard fairness benchmarks (such as StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs) to reveal logical failures and vague conceptualizations in how they define and measure stereotypes.
